error_description: The updateUser method creates PasswordEncoder local per request rather than as a singleton
The Article Constructor throws a NullPointerException if tagList is null or contains null elements
The favoriteArticle method doesnt saves the favorite article into database
The createArticle saves the articles with wrong data into database(title data into description)
Missing null check on user in findByArticleId → NullPointerException when called without user
Double encryption of the password using a password encoder in createUser method
userOptional.get() is called in method unfollow without first checking if a user was found → can throw NoSuchElementException
CreateUser logs include user passwords in plaintext - potentially exposing them in logs accessible to operators or attackers
The userLogin method creates PasswordEncoder local per request rather than as a singleton
Incorrect MIME/consume type in controller. The API expects JSON but text/plain is declared. Clients sending JSON may fail
The deleteComment method uses GET to delete data which violates HTTP rules and can cause security and consistency issues
The findUserFeedWithCursor calls articles.remove() which always fails with an IndexOutOfBoundsException because the provided index is outside the valid range
The unfavoriteArticle method saves articles instead of removing them
The findById method always tries to findById with index -1 instead of the passed id
The findByArticleIdWithCursor method attemptes to call isEmpty() on a null comments list -> NullPointer
The setLimit method is infinitely recursive -> continues consuming system resources until the application eventually crashes
findByUsername throws NullPointerException when userData is null. The crash happens at the first argument of the ProfileData constructor
The Comment Constructor sets the wrong value for the articleId
Logical fault: the save method checks for userId instead of article IDs -> executed every time which can lead to either duplicates or a runtime crash
The DefaultJwtSerice Constructor logs/prints the jwt secret to the console/logs
The toToken Method omitted the signWith() call -> parsing the token with parseClaimsJws(token) will throw a SignatureException because the parser expects a signed JWT
The isEmpty Method always returns true instead of checking for null and isEmpty -> possbile nullpointer
The canWriteArticle compares the user id with itself -> always true -> everyone can write articles
The articleComments method returns a Map<String/ArticleData> via dfe.getLocalContext but the code treats it directly as an ArticleData object -> causing a ClassCastException at runtime
The getCurrentUser method can crash on any non-standard authentication typically causing a NullPointerException or ClassCastException
The updateUser method writes the password into the bio and the bio into the password -> leaking passwords
The article endpoint produces text/plain instead of JSON which breaks interoperability with standard REST clients
Incorrect MIME type in the createArticle controller method. The API expects JSON but text/plain is declared. Clients sending JSON may fail
